intro: Lesson 48: Acids, alkalis, indicators and pH. Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: Phenolphthalein in sodium hydroxide solution is...
questions.a: B) Pink. Phenolphthalein is pink in alkali and colourless in acid.

questions.q: Write the ionic equation for neutralisation.
questions.model: Acids give H⁺, alkalis give OH⁻. They join to make water: H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O.

questions.q: Universal indicator turns orange. pH and type?
Name the salt made from HCl and NaOH.

Make red cabbage indicator at home with an adult and test vinegar, lemon juice, water, bicarbonate solution. Then answer: (a) classify each [2], (b) explain using ions what happens when bicarbonate solution is added to vinegar until neutral [2], (c) name an indicator that would be colourless in vinegar and pink in alkali [1], (d) give the approximate pH of vinegar [1].
questions.a: (a) vinegar, lemon acidic; water neutral; bicarbonate alkaline (2); (b) H⁺ from acid react with OH⁻ (or the base) (1) to form water; pH rises to 7 (1); (c) phenolphthalein (1); (d) about 3 (1)
questions.model: Teacher tests vinegar on camera: pink-red, so acidic.

questions.q: Explain why indigestion tablets contain bases.
questions.a: Excess stomach acid causes indigestion (1); the base neutralises the acid (1)

questions.q: Why is a pH 1 acid not ten times stronger than pH 2? Discuss the scale.
questions.a: Each pH unit is a tenfold change in H⁺ concentration, so pH 1 has ten times the H⁺ of pH 2 (the scale is logarithmic).
